label: Modal countermodel and exact support audit for independence and separability
summary: The unrestricted independence-to-modal-separability bridge fails in a concrete two-world universal-accessibility model with a necessary effect x: x depends on y, y does not depend on x, and both exist necessarily, so y cannot exist without x. This modal lifting matches the existing Lean omission-control truth tables for nonmutualDependenceSuffices_omit_hAllow; the extra modal interpretation was checked by finite truth-table evaluation, not a new Lean theorem. A co-variation model with contingent x also shows that contingency alone does not entail separability when dependence remains an unconstrained primitive. The registered graph has one direct consumer of the strong input, then a consumer deriving efficient-cause priority. The original terminal-only formula has no supports with this input forbidden, whereas taking the existing nonmutual-priority intermediate directly bypasses it. Exact three-input-to-one-input support substitution preserves 67,798,928 G and 109,971,456 H minimal families while shortening each package by two; unrestricted direct-or-derived support remains available. Full models, qualifications and graph equations: docs/notes/god-existence-support-formula.md, Scope audit.
blocker: To derive unrestricted nonmutual priority without the refuted bridge, establish a separate justified priority principle, or certify a contingent-effect modal bridge with explicit semantics and prove contingency at each relevant use site. Neither follows from the present primitive definitions alone.
